Climatic parameters per unit

Source: R/calc_par.R
calc_par.Rd

Computes summary statistics of each unit's series, such as the long-run mean and standard deviation of temperature, or the average yearly rainfall.

Usage

calc_par(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
calc_par(
  x,
  fn,
  period = NULL,
  min_coverage = 0.8,
  prefix = NULL,
  suffix = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A wide table from extract_*(), or a long table.

...

Further arguments of the methods; the table method takes none.

fn

The statistics: a named list of functions (list(avg = mean, total = sum)), a character vector of function names (c("mean", "sd")) or a single function. Functions receive the values with any NA, so handle them as needed (\(v) mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)).

period

NULL (all observations together), "year" or "month".

min_coverage

Number between 0 and 1: the share of a month's days that must be present for the month to count. Used only when period = "month".

prefix

Column name prefix; by default the variable, FALSE for none.

suffix

Optional column name suffix.

id

Optional name of the unit identifier column.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" splits the work by unit when it would not fit in memory; a whole number forces that many units per chunk; FALSE never splits.

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per unit: its identifiers and one column per statistic, registered with the statistic and period.

Details

With period, the statistics are first computed within each period and then averaged across periods: fn = list(total = sum), period = "year" gives the average yearly total. Periods are counted back from the last date of the data, so the last period always ends on the last observation: yearly periods are the 12-month windows ending there, monthly periods the one-month windows. When the last date is not the end of December (yearly) or of a month (monthly), a warning says so, because the windows then do not follow calendar years or months.

Columns are named <prefix>_<statistic>_<suffix>. The prefix defaults to the variable recorded upstream (announced), so a temperature table gives tmax_mean, tmax_sd.

Monthly coverage

With period = "month" a month represented by only a handful of days would enter the average as though it were complete. min_coverage guards against this by comparing the observations present in each window with the number of days it spans. If no month reaches it, the function stops; the most common cause is data already at monthly resolution, for which period = NULL or period = "year" are the right choices. Monthly input asked for monthly periods is refused at once.

Coefficient of variation of temperatures

A coefficient of variation divides by the mean, so it needs a scale with a true zero. Celsius and Fahrenheit have none: the same place would score differently in each, and a place averaging 0 C would divide by zero. Statistics named cv (or with cv as a word of their name, such as temp_cv), and cv() itself, are therefore computed on kelvin when the data are in C or F, with a message; the registry records ratio_unit = "K". The values look small, since the mean in the denominator is near 273 rather than 20. Data with no recorded unit whose variable is a temperature give a warning, because the scale is unknown.

See also

Other indicators: calc_condition(), calc_heatwave(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_std_index(), calc_std_threshold(), calc_threshold_day()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  ID = c(1, 2),
  `200101` = c(10, 20),
  `200102` = c(15, 25),
  `200201` = c(5, 15),
  `200202` = c(10, 20),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Mean across all observations
calc_par(df, fn = list(avg = mean))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#> # Context:  summary; key ID; 1 indicator
#>      ID   avg
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1    10
#> 2     2    20

# Average of yearly totals
calc_par(df, fn = list(total = sum), period = "year")
#> Warning: The last date (2002-02-01) is not the last day of a month and/or not in
#> December.
#> ℹ Yearly periods are the 12-month windows ending on it, not calendar years.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#> # Context:  summary; key ID; 1 indicator
#>      ID total
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1    20
#> 2     2    40
